description:
The price increases caused by President Donald Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran have made a lot of Americans unhappy with him. When he’s been asked about the inflation or the unhappiness, Trump has repeatedly responded with lies — fictional stories about how low prices supposedly were before the war.

The president has concocted a fantasy — of sub-$2 gas, sub-2% inflation, and generally reduced prices — that bears little resemblance to the actual state of the country prior to the first strikes against Iran on February 28. CNN's "NewsNight" panel debates, and CNN's Matt Egan breaks down current gas prices, which have hit a wartime high.

author: CNN
description:
The sticker shock on Memorial Day, the unofficial start of the summer driving season, adds to the cost-of-living frustrations that have soured voters on the Trump economy. 

GasBuddy, a crowdsourced fuel price platform, expects the national average will be about $4.48 a gallon this Memorial Day. That would be 42% above the price last Memorial Day and the second-highest on record, according to GasBuddy. 

The only time gas was more expensive on Memorial Day was in 2022 when the average was $4.61 a gallon in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. 

CNN Business senior reporter Matt Egan looks at rising energy costs for Americans as President Trump downplays it as “peanuts” compared to the threat of Iran’s nuclear program. Also, CNN global economic analyst Rana Foroohar details the impact rising costs may have on the midterm elections. 

0:00 CNN’s Matt Egan on spiking gas prices ahead of Memorial Day weekend 
2:00 How much more are American families spending on energy since Iran war
title: Gas prices: Trump says ‘peanuts’. Could they hit all-time Memorial Day high?

author: CNN
description:
The unprecedented lawsuit President Donald Trump brought against the Internal Revenue Service over the unauthorized disclosure of his tax returns years ago has led to an unprecedented arrangement that will make nearly $1.8 billion in taxpayer funds available to allies of the president who say they were unfairly investigated by the government in the past.

The announcement of the “Anti-Weaponization Fund” and the agreement the IRS can’t bring claims against Trump, his family or businesses for past tax issues have immediately drawn criticism from Democrats, public interest groups and former government officials who say that Trump is using the levers of the government he controls to set up a vast piggybank for his supporters and protect himself.

The panelists on CNN NewsNight, led by Sara Sidner, share a series of heated debates over the purpose of the fund.

1:03 'Are these reparations?'
5:49 Dr. Cornel West predicts how this all plays out
